Indigenous Health Assessment (Adult 15–54 Years)

Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:
  • Dysuria, urinary frequency, pink-tinged urine, suprapubic ache for ≈1 week – clinician impression: uncomplicated urinary tract infection (UTI/cystitis).  
  • Possible pregnancy risk acknowledged (sex 1–2 weeks ago, on combined pill, last menstrual period 2 weeks ago).  
  • Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) – long-standing, variable stool pattern.

- Relevant family medical history: Not recorded (patient denied bladder/kidney disease; no other conditions discussed).

- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):
  • Combined oral contraceptive pill (brand/dose not documented).  
  • Mebeverine (antispasmodic for IBS) – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  • Paracetamol advised PRN for pain (new recommendation).

- Immunisation status reviewed: Not recorded.

- Sexual and reproductive health:
  • Sexually active with long-term boyfriend; generally does not use condoms.  
  • On combined oral contraceptive pill.  
  • Last unprotected intercourse ≈1 week ago.  
  • Last menstrual period: 2 weeks ago.  
  • No unusual vaginal discharge reported.

- Physical activity and nutrition: Not recorded.

- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use:
  • Alcohol: drinks socially.  
  • Tobacco: does not smoke cigarettes.  
  • Cannabis: smoked once ≈1.5 weeks ago at a party; advised against regular use.

- Hearing loss or concerns: Not recorded.

- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk): Not recorded.

- Vision problems or recent changes: Not recorded.

- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities:
  • Lives in university halls with a flatmate; family live nearby and supportive.  
  • University student studying English; adjusting well to course.

Examination

- BP, pulse rate and rhythm: Not recorded (telehealth).
- Height, weight, BMI, waist circumference: Not recorded.
- Oral exam (including dentition and gums): Not performed.
- Ear exam (otoscopy, whisper test if needed): Not performed.
- Vision/eye exam (basic screen): Not performed.
- Urinalysis (dipstick for proteinuria): Planned but not yet done.

Investigations (as indicated)

- Mid-stream urine (MSU) for microscopy, culture, sensitivity – specimen to be dropped at clinic (ordered).
- Other routine adult screening (BGL, lipids, cervical screening, STI screen, etc.): Not ordered/discussed at this visit.

Management Plan

- Suspected uncomplicated UTI: commence empirical oral antibiotics (Trimethoprim or Nitrofurantoin 3-day course – specific agent to be dispensed per clinician decision).  
- Provide MSU container and instructions; patient to drop sample to clinic today; results to guide/confirm therapy.  
- Hydration advice: increase oral fluids.  
- Symptomatic relief: paracetamol as needed.  
- Safety-netting: return or call earlier if develops fever, flank/back pain, vomiting, or if no improvement within 1 week.  
- Discussed low likelihood that single cannabis use is related to UTI; advised avoiding further use.  
- Pregnancy consideration noted; no immediate test arranged – re-assess if treatment failure or period late.

Considerations for future/ongoing care
- Preventive screening: cervical screening when eligible (age ≥25); STI screen due to unprotected sex (age 19).  
- Immunisation review (e.g., influenza, COVID-19, HPV completion).  
- CTG registration and Aboriginal Health Check items at next face-to-face visit, if applicable.

Quality checks

● Missing but clinically expected elements: BP, pulse, height/weight/BMI, waist circumference, immunisation review, mental health screening, alcohol/smoking quantity details, hearing and vision screening, detailed medication doses, allergy reaction details, cervical/STI screening discussion, substance use counseling documentation.  
● Internal contradictions: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear audio; minimal interruptions; some informal language but clinical content understandable.
